prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the exact same root cause: when SSE reconnection in `_handle_reconnection` exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, nothing currently signals failure back to whatever is awaiting the original request's response, so that call hangs forever. #2395 fixes this by constructing a JSON-RPC INTERNAL_ERROR response tied to the original request id and sending it through `read_stream_writer`, failing only the affected request while the rest of the connection stays alive; the diff also drops the `# pragma: no cover` marker on that branch, indicating new test coverage was added for it. #3098 instead defines a `StreamableHTTPError` and a `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull it out of anyio `ExceptionGroup`s so a raised exception propagates to the top-level `async with streamablehttp_client()` caller. Since (per the diff shown) this exception would be raised inside the task group handling the shared connection, it would tear down the whole transport (all in-flight requests) rather than failing just the one affected request — a materially different, more disruptive failure mode for the same bug. (2 PRs)

prs.author: Whning0513
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs rewrite WWW-Authenticate header parsing in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py to fix incorrect/substring parameter matching, replacing whatever naive regex or string-search logic previously extracted auth-params (e.g. resource_metadata, scope) from the header. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs rewrite WWW-Authenticate header parsing in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py to fix incorrect/substring parameter matching, replacing whatever naive regex or string-search logic previously extracted auth-params (e.g. resource_metadata, scope) from the header. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a comma-splitting tokenizer that respects quoted strings and escaped characters, but #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the ENTIRE header on top-level commas and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the 'Bearer' scheme token and stops collecting params when a new scheme token appears. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of comma-separated params, with no scheme-boundary detection. This means #3012 would incorrectly merge parameters from a second challenge (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="invalid_token"') into the Bearer result, while #3041's segment-then-scan approach correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params in multi-challenge headers, which is the RFC 7235-correct behavior. #3041 is also the larger, more complete diff (88 vs 45 lines) covering this multi-scheme case explicitly.

It also adds an issuer-binding check to validate rediscovered metadata and an eager_discovery_attempted flag specifically to avoid re-probing a metadata-less server on every in-process refresh, covering a case #2492's persistence-only approach does not address.

members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the exact same root cause: when SSE reconnection in `_handle_reconnection` exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, nothing currently signals failure back to whatever is awaiting the original request's response, so that call hangs forever. #2395 fixes this by constructing a JSON-RPC INTERNAL_ERROR response tied to the original request id and sending it through `read_stream_writer`, failing only the affected request while the rest of the connection stays alive; the diff also drops the `# pragma: no cover` marker on that branch, indicating new test coverage was added for it. #3098 instead defines a `StreamableHTTPError` and a `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull it out of anyio `ExceptionGroup`s so a raised exception propagates to the top-level `async with streamablehttp_client()` caller. Since (per the diff shown) this exception would be raised inside the task group handling the shared connection, it would tear down the whole transport (all in-flight requests) rather than failing just the one affected request — a materially different, more disruptive failure mode for the same bug. clusters.pick_reason: Both add a comma-splitting tokenizer that respects quoted strings and escaped characters, but #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the ENTIRE header on top-level commas and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the 'Bearer' scheme token and stops collecting params when a new scheme token appears. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of comma-separated params, with no scheme-boundary detection. This means #3012 would incorrectly merge parameters from a second challenge (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="invalid_token"') into the Bearer result, while #3041's segment-then-scan approach correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params in multi-challenge headers, which is the RFC 7235-correct behavior. #3041 is also the larger, more complete diff (88 vs 45 lines) covering this multi-scheme case explicitly.

members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both PRs touch the same two lines in stdio_server() that create the read/write anyio memory object streams, and both aim to relieve blocking/backpressure caused by those streams being unbuffered (size 0). #2215 exposes read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as caller-supplied parameters but defaults both to 0, so out-of-the-box behavior — including write-side blocking during progress notifications — is unchanged unless a caller opts in. #2654 instead hardcodes the write_stream buffer to 1 and ships a BlockingStdout test reproducing a handler queuing its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier progress notification, directly fixing the default-path stall. members.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
members.author: Dharit13
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the exact same root cause: when SSE reconnection in `_handle_reconnection` exhausts MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS, nothing currently signals failure back to whatever is awaiting the original request's response, so that call hangs forever. #2395 fixes this by constructing a JSON-RPC INTERNAL_ERROR response tied to the original request id and sending it through `read_stream_writer`, failing only the affected request while the rest of the connection stays alive; the diff also drops the `# pragma: no cover` marker on that branch, indicating new test coverage was added for it. #3098 instead defines a `StreamableHTTPError` and a `_unwrap_exception` helper to pull it out of anyio `ExceptionGroup`s so a raised exception propagates to the top-level `async with streamablehttp_client()` caller. Since (per the diff shown) this exception would be raised inside the task group handling the shared connection, it would tear down the whole transport (all in-flight requests) rather than failing just the one affected request — a materially different, more disruptive failure mode for the same bug. (2 PRs)

clusters.pick_reason: Both add a comma-splitting tokenizer that respects quoted strings and escaped characters, but #3041's _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the ENTIRE header on top-level commas and then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the 'Bearer' scheme token and stops collecting params when a new scheme token appears. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead finds only the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one flat list of comma-separated params, with no scheme-boundary detection. This means #3012 would incorrectly merge parameters from a second challenge (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="invalid_token"') into the Bearer result, while #3041's segment-then-scan approach correctly isolates only the Bearer challenge's params in multi-challenge headers, which is the RFC 7235-correct behavior. #3041 is also the larger, more complete diff (88 vs 45 lines) covering this multi-scheme case explicitly.
